newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says 67 soldiers, rebels killed in north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says 67 soldiers, rebels killed in north.

text.p: Sri Lankan government troops clashed with a large group of Tamil Tiger rebels in the north of the country, killing at least 50 guerrillas, the military said on Friday.
The Defence Ministry said in a statement that one officer and 16 soldiers were also killed in the gunbattle with the group of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels on Thursday.
Troops operating southwest of Nedunkerni town were attacked by the rebels using artillery and mortars, the statement said. Troops then retaliated, it added.
Nedunkerni lies some 40 km (25 miles) northeast of the government-held town of Vavuniya, which is some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
Troops had called in helicopter gunships to engage the rebels, who fled northwards with their casualties, the statement said.
Ground troops confirmed at least 50 rebels were killed and more than 30 wounded, the statement said. Fourteen soldiers were also wounded in the fighting.
There was no immediate statement from the LTTE on the clash.
Sri Lankan troops launched a major offensive against the rebels in the northern Wanni region in May to open a strategic highway to link the northern Jaffna peninsula with the rest of the island.
Two fierce counter-attacks by the rebels in June have slowed down the advance, but the soldiers carry out daily operations in the region.
The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, which erupted in 1983. The LTTE puts the toll higher.
